lena: Quick sync: we need to pick a pattern for tenant egress IP preservation for Private customers. two contenders: regional shared relay (one relay per region, SNATed) vs per-tenant ENI/NAT (dedicated egress IP per tenant).

carlos: TL;DR: shared relay wins on cost/scale, per-tenant ENI wins on ACLs + compliance.

ev an: nit: per-tenant ENI has two sub-options: colocated connector in customer VPC (we already support) or attach customer-specific ENIs in our subnet via cross-account peering. both add ops complexity.

lena: list tradeoffs so PMs can decide: cost, ops, rollout, certs, monitoring, failover.

carlos: cost: shared relay amortizes GPUs/instances. per-tenant ENI requires more IPs, ENI limits, cross-account roles. ops: shared relay is simpler (one fleet), per-tenant ENI -> infra+quota management.

ev an: security/compliance: per-tenant ENI gives true source IP (no header shims), customer can apply IP-based allowlists. with shared relay you either SNAT or rely on signed X headers (application-level).

sofia: observability: with shared relay we can instrument per-token latency/cost centrally. per-tenant ENI scatters telemetry; we need log aggregation and tenant tagging. both doable but extra plumbing for ENI.

lena: cert rotation and mTLS: shared relay must proxy many tenant certs. two modes: SNI passthrough vs terminate & re-origin. per-tenant ENI keeps TLS end-to-end so rotation remains customer's problem.

carlos: rollback story: shared relay rollback is a single deploy. ENI path requires rolling back many attachments -> higher blast radius but limited per-tenant.

ev an: ops constraints: cloud provider ENI quotas are real. at scale we hit limits and request slowness on attach/detach. also cross-account route churn can cause transient blackholes.

lena: edge cases: 1) non-TLS protocols (grpc with no SNI), 2) customers who need exact source port for legacy ACLs, 3) customers behind provider-grade NAT where source is already altered.

sofia: mitigation ideas: - hybrid: default to shared relay, offer per-tenant ENI as enterprise add-on. - signed header (X-Redwood-Auth) for apps that only need IP for logging. - managed colocated connector for strict compliance customers.

carlos: implement checklist if we pick hybrid: 1) gating UI + billing flag, 2) ENI attach automation + quota monitoring, 3) SLO for attach/detach time, 4) docs for customer network teams.

ev an: perf note: per-tenant ENI reduces one hop and SNAT overhead -> latency wins, but network egress cost may be higher depending on topology (cross-account NAT).

lena: concrete next steps: - spike ENI attach automation (evan) 5d - prototype signed header and verification libs (carlos) 2d - costing model + limits spreadsheet (lena) 3d

lena: agreed. I'll assemble a one-pager and link spikes. thanks everyone. :party_parrot:
